title: Mayonnaise
description: A classic French cold emulsified mother sauce made from egg yolk, neutral oil, mustard, and lemon juice or vinegar, forming the base for countless dressings, dips, and derivative sauces.

ingredients.title: For the Mayonnaise
items: Neutral oil (vegetable or grapeseed) – 150 ml (⅔ cup)
Fresh lemon juice or white wine vinegar – 1–2 tsp

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Base
steps: Place the egg yolk, Dijon mustard, and a pinch of salt into a mixing bowl.
Whisk until the mixture is smooth and well combined.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Creating the Emulsion
steps: Slowly drizzle in the neutral oil while whisking constantly to create a stable emulsion.
Once the mixture begins to thicken, continue adding the remaining oil in a thin, steady stream.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Seasoning
steps: Whisk in the lemon juice or white wine vinegar until the desired acidity is reached.
Season with salt and white pepper, adjusting the mustard or lemon juice if desired.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Finishing
steps: Transfer the mayonnaise to a clean container.
Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Use as the base for Aioli, Tartar Sauce, or Rémoulade.
Mix into potato salad, coleslaw, or pasta salad.
Serve as a dip for seafood, fries, or fresh vegetables.

chefTips: Ensure all ingredients are at room temperature for a stable emulsion.
Add the oil very slowly at the beginning to prevent the mayonnaise from splitting.
If the mayonnaise breaks, whisk a fresh egg yolk in a clean bowl and gradually incorporate the split mixture.
Use a neutral-flavored oil for a smooth, balanced taste.
Store refrigerated and use within 2–3 days if made with raw egg.
